diagnostic_evidence.quote: In \eqref{eq_recur_F}, the partial derivatives $\partial_{\theta}$ also act on $F_s^{\Upsilon_i}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def_elediff prescribes that in the operator product $(F^{\Upsilon_1}_s\cdot\partial_\theta)\cdots(F^{\Upsilon_l}_s\cdot\partial_\theta)F_t(s,\Theta_s)$ the derivatives also differentiate the factors $F_s^{\Upsilon_i}$ (nested first-order operators). Nested directional derivatives do not commute: $(u\cdot\partial)(v\cdot\partial)F-(v\cdot\partial)(u\cdot\partial)F=(u_a\partial_a v_b-v_a\partial_a u_b)\partial_bF\neq0$ for generic data. Hence for equivalent trees $\Upsilon=(\Upsilon_1\Upsilon_2)_k$ and $\Upsilon'=(\Upsilon_2\Upsilon_1)_k$ one has $F^{\Upsilon}_{t,s}\neq F^{\Upsilon'}_{t,s}$ in general, so claim (iii) of prop_Labs_equ is false under the paper's own convention. Conversely, the proof of thm_taylor requires the opposite (frozen/multilinear) convention: the Taylor terms $(R^{n,j}\cdot\partial_\theta)^lF_{t_{n,i}}(t_{n,j},\Theta_{t_{n,j}})$ have constant direction vectors, so the multinomial expansion (eq_defIi) yields symmetric multilinear forms; the identification in eq_defGijl with eq_recur_F and the permutation grouping are valid only if the derivatives do NOT act on the $F^{\Upsilon_i}$. As written, the ULN-tree quantities $F^{\dbr{\Upsilon}}$ (def_func_Ntree, whose well-definedness is said to follow from prop_Labs_equ) are ill-defined and thm_taylor's proof is invalid.

failure_location.quote: \item[(iii)] $F_{t}^{\Upsilon} = F_{t}^{\Upsilon^{\prime}}$, $F_{t, s}^{\Upsilon} = F_{t, s}^{\Upsilon^{\prime}}$ for $s \in (t, T]$, $t \in [0, T)$;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the elementary differentials with frozen (multilinear) coefficients, e.g. $F^{(\Upsilon_1\cdots\Upsilon_l)_k}_{t,s}=\partial_s^k\E[\partial_\theta^lF_t(s,\Theta_s)[F^{\Upsilon_1}_s,\ldots,F^{\Upsilon_l}_s]|\F_t]$, delete/correct the remark in def_elediff, and read the operator powers in eq_defIi as frozen multinomials; then prop_Labs_equ(iii) holds and the proof's identifications go through.
issues.overall_effect: The well-definedness of elementary differentials on ULN-trees, prop_Labs_equ(iii), and the proof of the error expansion thm_taylor (and hence the written proofs of thm_consistent and the convergence results, though their conclusions are re-derivable once the convention is corrected) are unreliable as written.
issues.title: Elementary-differential convention (derivatives acting on branch factors) contradicts branch-permutation invariance
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local convention change that preserves all statements and needs no new lemma, but as written a stated proposition is false, the central definition prescribes the wrong object, and the main proof's key identifications must be re-verified under the corrected convention — a contained but non-routine correction, not a typo fix.

issues.failure_explanation: In step (iv) of the proof, the sum over ordered tuples $(\Upsilon_1,\ldots,\Upsilon_l)$ is regrouped as $\sum_{\Upsilon\in\widetilde\T(r)}N_P(\Upsilon)B_i^m(\Upsilon)$ (eq_tildeIi). For fixed $k,l$ the map from ordered tuples to LN-trees $(\Upsilon_1\cdots\Upsilon_l)_k$ is a bijection, so the ordered-tuple sum equals $\sum_{\Upsilon}B_i^m(\Upsilon)$ with no extra multiplicity; the inserted factor $N_P(\Upsilon)$ (number of branch permutations fixing the branch list) is wrong. Consequently the closed-form coefficient $\frac{\alpha S}{\gamma}A_j^m$ ($=\prod_v 1/k_v!$) overstates the true Taylor coefficients by $\prod_v N_P(v)$ for any tree with a node carrying repeated branches. Concretely, for $\Upsilon=[[\;]_0[\;]_0]_0$ the direct Taylor computation gives the coefficient $\frac12\sum_j a_{ij}A_j^m([\;]_0)^2=\frac12 A_i^m(\Upsilon)$ (the $1/2!$ from Taylor, and only one ordered tuple $(B,B)$ exists since the branches are identical), whereas the theorem claims $\frac{\alpha S}{\gamma}A_i^m=\frac{1\cdot2}{2}A_i^m=A_i^m$ — a factor of 2. The stated expansion is therefore false for every tree containing a symmetric node.

failure_location.quote: R^{n, j} = \sum_{\Upsilon \in \T_r} \frac{\alpha\br{\Upsilon} S\br{\Upsilon}}{\gamma\br{\Upsilon}} A_j^m\br{\Upsilon} \br{\Delta t_n}^{\abs{\Upsilon}} F_{t_{n, j}}^{\Upsilon} + \mO\br{\br{\Delta t}^{r+1}}, \quad \Delta t \to 0

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the spurious $N_P$ factor in the grouping step and re-derive the closed form: the correct coefficient is $\prod_v 1/(k_v!\,N_P(v))$ instead of $\frac{\alpha S}{\gamma}=\prod_v 1/k_v!$, yielding a comparable corrected theorem via the same proof.
issues.overall_effect: The precise error expansion of thm_taylor (advertised as one of the main results) has incorrect coefficients for symmetric trees. The order conditions (tab_ordcond, C(r), prop_Cr_table) and thm_consistent/thm_converge/coro_error_est are unaffected, since they use only the fact that the tree coefficients are nonzero multiples of $A_0^m(\Upsilon)$.
issues.title: Erroneous symmetry factor: expansion coefficients of trees with repeated branches are overstated
issues.why_classification: A main stated theorem is false as written (wrong constants for symmetric trees), but a recognizably comparable version follows from the same proof architecture with corrected multiplicity bookkeeping — a contained re-derivation with no loss of scope or rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: F_{t}(s, \theta) := \vbr{\bigg}{f(s, X_s, \theta), f(s, X_s, \theta) \frac{\Delta W_{t, s}^{\top}}{s - t}}, \;\;\; \theta \in \R^p \times \R^{p \times q}
R^{n, i} = \mO\br{\Delta t_n}, \quad i = m, m-1, \cdots, 0.

issues.failure_explanation: The second component of $F_t(s,\theta)$ contains $\Delta W_{t,s}^\top/(s-t)$, which is of typical size $(s-t)^{-1/2}$ and is a.s. unbounded, so no uniform bound on $F$ or its $\theta$-derivatives exists. Nevertheless: (i) the a.s. prior estimate $R^{n,i}=O(\Delta t_n)$ (eq_preest_Rni) is asserted with no argument — bounding $\E[\Delta F^{n,j}_{t_{n,i}}|\F_{t_{n,i}}]$ requires controlling conditional expectations of $f$-differences multiplied by $\Delta W/h$, for which Cauchy–Schwarz yields only $O(h^{-1/2})$; (ii) the Taylor remainder in eq_EtniDelFninj is claimed to be $O(|\Delta t_n|^r)$ 'from eq_preest_Rni', but with $R^{n,j}=O(h)$ and $\partial_\theta^rF\sim h^{-1/2}$ the standard remainder estimate gives $O(h^{r-1/2})$, not $O(h^r)$; recovering $O(h^r)$ requires a Gaussian integration-by-parts cancellation that is never established. Similarly, the existence of the limits $F^{\Upsilon}_t=\lim_{s\to t+}F^{\Upsilon}_{t,s}$, the boundedness of the elementary differentials, and the uniformity in $n$ (used in eq_taylor_Ftninj and claimed in the theorem) are not proven. These estimates are the analytic core of the consistency analysis.

failure_location.quote: for $j = m, m-1, \cdots, i+1$, where the remainder term follows from \eqref{eq_preest_Rni}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply lemmas (under Assumption assu_regu, via Gaussian integration by parts / smoothness of the conditional-expectation functionals of the diffusion) establishing the a.s. boundedness of the relevant conditional expectations involving $\Delta W/(s-t)$, the $O(h^r)$ Taylor remainders, the existence and boundedness of the elementary differentials $F^{\Upsilon}_{t,s}$ and their limits, all uniformly in $n$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm_taylor is incomplete as written; since thm_consistent is derived from thm_taylor and thm_converge/coro_error_est from thm_consistent, the entire consistency and convergence chain is unproven as written (though the statements are plausible under Assumption 1).
issues.title: Unjustified remainder estimates for the singular $\Delta W_{t,s}/(s-t)$ kernel
issues.why_classification: The missing arguments are nontrivial (they constitute the technical heart of BSDE scheme analysis) but are contained and standard-in-kind under the strong smoothness assumptions; no new global proof architecture or weakening of the results is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assumption~\ref{assu_FLipVar} is introduced for technical reason.
The following Lemma~\ref{lemm_fnoz} shows that Assumption~\ref{assu_FLipVar} can be fulfilled if $f\br{t, x, y, z}$ is uniformly Lipschitz w.r.t.  $y$ and is independent of $z$.
We should remark that in Corollary~\ref{coro_error_est}, the conditions on $f$ is sufficient but not necessary for the convergence of \Cref{sch_rk}.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion asserts, without qualification, that stability and convergence of the proposed schemes are rigorously proved. What is actually proved: thm_rk_stable and thm_converge/coro_error_est hold only under the technical Assumption assu_FLipVar, which is verified (lemm_fnoz, lemm_linearf) only for generators independent of $z$ (Lipschitz in $y$) or linear in $(y,z)$. The schemes are proposed for general generators, and the paper's own numerical examples use $f$ nonlinear in $z$ (e.g. the $z^2$ term in Example 1), outside the proved regime. The prose thus claims a scope — unconditional rigorous convergence of the proposed schemes — that the formal content does not support.

failure_location.quote: Based on this theory, we also rigorously prove the stability, and convergence of the proposed schemes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the conclusion sentence, e.g. 'under additional structural assumptions on the generator (Assumption 3), we rigorously prove stability and convergence'.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's summary of its own guarantees overstates the coverage of the stability/convergence theory relative to the stated conditional results.
issues.title: Conclusion overclaims unconditional rigorous stability and convergence proofs
issues.why_classification: A prose qualification fixes the overclaim; no formal result, rate, or advertised scope of the theorems themselves is altered.
